system.description:
Starting at 18th level, you learn the ultimate molding for working with your Bonded summons called Synchronization Technique.

Synchronization Technique. You spend 2 Focus and command each Bonded creature to spend their reaction and 4 Jutsu Slots to embolden the jutsu cast. When you do, yourself and all Bonded creatures unite around this single jutsu. Each Bonded creature must cast a Jutsu it knows of the lowest rank it can cast, relying on your initial jutsu. If the triggering jutsu scores a hit or at least one of the affected creatures to fail their saving throws your Bonded creatures jutsu to apply their effects as if they scored a hit or the creature also failed their saving throws vs their jutsu.

Once you use this molding, you cannot do so again for 10 minutes

| #### Design Note(s) / Summoner / The Summoner subclass that you see before you is built currently in a non-final state. This is primarily due to its direct connection to Sage Beast Tribes, their features, their levels, and how they grow and scale / Summons currently grow at 6 ASI’s per rank, are levels 4/8/12/16.20, and have a heap of other benefits, such as a Primary offensive score and primary defensive score, passive attack effects, and certain tribes having extremely strong abilities. / The Training Document Summons as they have been presented to you are an attempt to reign in their power and make them support creatures, instead of force multipliers. The changes made were; / Levels Scaled back to 2/5/9/13/17 / Reduction of ASI’s down to +3 per rank. / Removal of Defensive Ability Score / Reduction of Jutsu Slots across all casting tiers. / While the above does reign in their power a lot, there are some things that can still be adjusted for Non-Summoner Subclass, players who want to summon a creature, so that they are support creatures and not combat warping. / This means that if Summons for normal players are meant to be support based in terms of their capabilities without being combat warping, then that means for a Summoner (and all Summoner like subclasses moving forward) should be primarily be able to rely on their summon to be a constant force to recognize. |
